prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Business Rules Registry(BRR): thresholds, validation thresholds, reason codes, exception rules per mode, connection/gate/towing/stand/swap rules, border states, CTT tolerance, freeze horizon, tie-breaker. Modes: Normal; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction(binding metering; RFM may suspend swaps); Recovery; Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms); Contingency Fallback(ADM declares after RFM, Tower Supervisor, SSE). Fallback: Foxglove down→Digital Briefing Room; Marlinstone/CAM unreliable→last verified Airport Capacity Plan(ACP); Blueharbor down→Slot Coordinator manual sheet at Contingency Operations Console, keeps last CTT; revised CTT needs Tower Supervisor+Ramp Control Lead, AOC readback; Ironleaf advisory; Emberline monitor-only. Regional Flow Platform(RFP) reconciles with Collaborative Decision Log on restore. Identity Access Service authoritative roles; least privilege; no shared accounts; separation of duties for GDP/AAR/Tactical Regulation Proposal; emergency access via Silverpine needs incident ref+expiry. Tower Supervisor runs Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Control Lead runs Ramp Movement Board. Audit Event Ledger logs auth, approvals, config, exports, emergency access, slot compliance, discrepancy dispositions. Slot compliance: CTT/TOBT/AOBT/ATOT compared; Performance Analytics Warehouse aggregates; Post Operations Report. Ownership: Meteorology Briefing Officer owns weather classification inputs to Weather Ingest Gateway; Airline Operations Coordinator(AOC) accountable for schedule intent, readiness, TOBT updates; data elements need meaning, range, update authority, retention, escalation contact. Common Situation Display shows freshness (last update, max age, current/aging/stale/unavailable); Time Synchronization Service gives time basis. Demand Prediction Service, CAM, Slot Allocation Engine, Departure Metering Service reject untrusted-timestamp data. Validation: schema, mandatory, code set, temporal, plausibility. Flight Data Exchange validates Flight Intent Message; Surface Surveillance Adapter marks uncertain positions; Airline Interface Adapter carrier format checks; Handling Resource Planner validates resources. Discrepancy: mark disputed, keep prior value; Data Governance Steward resolves; urgent via Alert Distribution Hub, reviewed in Digital Briefing Room; SSE investigates technical causes.

New part:
S836: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall retain data quality measures, including validation failure rates, freshness breaches, manual corrections, and recurring ownership conflicts.
S837: Stewardship reviews shall use those measures to update training, adjust validation rules, and improve the reliability of information used in operational decision making.
S838: Performance measurement for the Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System shall convert operational events into repeatable indicators that can be reviewed after each operating day.
S839: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall calculate delay absorption as the portion of expected airborne or terminal-area delay that is converted into controlled ground delay before departure.
S840: Delay absorption shall be measured by comparing the unconstrained demand predicted by the Demand Prediction Service with the regulated demand produced by the Slot Allocation Engine and the realized movement times captured through the Flight Data Exchange.
S841: The principal delay absorption indicator shall report minutes absorbed at origin, minutes remaining in the arrival stream, and minutes transferred to surface queues within the region.
S842: The Regional Flow Manager shall use this indicator to verify that a Ground Delay Program reduced airborne holding without creating excessive departure congestion at constrained airports.
S843: Queue length performance shall be measured for runway departure queues, arrival metering queues, apron movement queues, and regulation waiting lists.
S844: The Tower Sequence Manager shall provide runway sequence counts, while the Ramp Movement Board shall provide surface queue counts based on movement status and surveillance confirmation.
S845: The North Runway Meter, South Runway Meter, East Apron Sensor, and West Apron Sensor shall support independent checks of queue length where surveillance coverage is available.
S846: Queue metrics shall include maximum queue length, average queue length, time above threshold, and recovery time after a constraint is lifted.
S847: Slot adherence shall be measured as the difference between actual movement times and the assigned Calculated Takeoff Time or Target Off Block Time.
S848: The Slot Coordinator shall review slot adherence by operator, airport, time band, and regulation identifier to detect recurring causes of noncompliance.
S849: A flight shall be counted within tolerance when the actual takeoff or off-block event occurs inside the operating window defined in the Business Rules Registry.
S850: The Slot Compliance State shall be used to identify periods when adherence monitoring has operational priority over advisory optimization.
S851: The Departure Metering Service uses the Passenger Misconnect Count to weight departure sequencing decisions when connection protection is an approved local objective.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
